title: Thermodynamics — 40 MCQs
description: Covers thermodynamic systems and processes, the second law of thermodynamics, heat engines, Otto, Diesel and Carnot cycles, refrigerators, and entropy and disorder.

questions.q: A thermodynamic system is
options: any region of the universe under consideration
questions.explanation: A thermodynamic system is a definite portion of matter or space chosen for study, separated from the surroundings by a boundary.

questions.q: An isolated system can exchange
options: both matter and energy with surroundings
neither matter nor energy with surroundings
questions.explanation: An isolated system is completely sealed and insulated; neither matter nor energy can cross its boundary.

questions.q: The second law of thermodynamics states that
options: heat flows spontaneously from a hotter to a colder body
entropy of an isolated system can decrease
work can be completely converted into heat
questions.explanation: One statement of the second law is that heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder to a hotter body.

questions.q: A heat engine converts
options: part of the heat absorbed into work
questions.explanation: No heat engine can convert all absorbed heat into work; some heat is always rejected to a sink.

questions.q: The efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between temperatures T₁ and T₂ (T₁ > T₂) is
questions.explanation: η_Carnot = 1 − T₂/T₁ where temperatures are in kelvin.

questions.q: In a refrigerator heat is extracted from
options: the hot body and rejected to the cold body
the cold body and rejected to the hot body
questions.explanation: A refrigerator removes heat from a cold interior and rejects it to the warmer surroundings.

questions.q: Entropy is a measure of
options: disorder or randomness in a system
questions.explanation: Entropy quantifies the degree of molecular disorder or the number of microscopic configurations.

questions.q: The working substance in a Carnot engine is usually
questions.explanation: The classical Carnot cycle is analysed using an ideal gas as the working substance.

questions.q: The Otto cycle is the ideal cycle for
questions.explanation: The Otto cycle models the processes in a spark-ignition (petrol) internal-combustion engine.

questions.q: The Diesel cycle is the ideal cycle for
questions.explanation: The Diesel cycle approximates the processes in a compression-ignition diesel engine.

questions.q: According to the second law, the entropy of an isolated system
questions.explanation: The entropy of an isolated system can only increase or remain constant; it never decreases.

questions.q: A Carnot refrigerator extracts 200 J of heat from a cold body. If its COP is 4 the work input required is
questions.explanation: COP = Q₂/W ⇒ W = Q₂/COP = 200/4 = 50 J.

questions.q: In the Carnot cycle the processes are
questions.explanation: The Carnot cycle consists of reversible isothermal expansion, adiabatic expansion, isothermal compression and adiabatic compression.

questions.q: The statement “It is impossible to construct a device that operates in a cycle and produces no effect other than the transfer of heat from a colder to a hotter body” is known as
questions.explanation: This is the Clausius statement of the second law of thermodynamics.

questions.q: The Kelvin-Planck statement of the second law asserts that
options: a heat engine cannot have 100 % efficiency
heat cannot flow from cold to hot
questions.explanation: It is impossible for a heat engine to convert heat completely into work without rejecting some heat to a sink.

questions.q: For an ideal gas the change in entropy in an isothermal reversible expansion is
questions.explanation: ΔS = Q_rev/T = nRT ln(V₂/V₁)/T = nR ln(V₂/V₁).

questions.explanation: In the ideal Diesel cycle heat addition occurs at constant pressure.

questions.explanation: In the ideal Otto cycle heat addition occurs at constant volume.

questions.explanation: ΔU = Q − W = 500 − 200 = 300 J (first law).

questions.explanation: The third law of thermodynamics states that the entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero as T → 0 K.
